1-2.word_for_word: catuḥtriṃśe — in chapter thirty-four; ahinā grastam nandam hariḥ amūmucat — Hari freed Nanda who had been seized by a serpent; vidyādharam ca aṅgiraḥ-śāpāt — and released a Vidyādhara from the curse of the Āṅgirasa sages; śaṅkhacūḍam tathā avadhīt — and later killed Śaṅkhacūḍa; rāsa-apadeśataḥ kāmam kiṅkarī-kṛtya — having made desire itself a servant through the rāsa episode; kāmataḥ anugṛhṇan — while granting grace according to longing; vaśam ninye tathā vidyādhara-adhipam — he similarly brought the lord of the Vidyādharas under control; kāma-anugraha-mukhena kāma-jayam pratipādya — after teaching the conquest of desire through the mode of grace toward desire; vidyādhara-jayam pratipādayitum — he now shows the conquest of a Vidyādhara
1-2.translation: In the thirty-fourth chapter Hari frees Nanda, who had been swallowed by a serpent; he releases the Vidyādhara Sudarśana from the curse of the Āṅgirasa sages; and he later kills Śaṅkhacūḍa. Having just demonstrated his conquest of desire through the rāsa narrative—even making kāma itself serve his purpose while granting grace according to the devotees' longing—the text now introduces a related episode displaying his mastery over the lord of the Vidyādharas.

3.word_for_word: gāvaḥ — cows; gāḥ — cows; madhu — sweet; madhu-annam — food accompanied by honey
3.translation: The gloss identifies the offerings: ‘gāvaḥ’ means cows, and ‘madhu-annam’ is sweet food, food served together with honey.

4.word_for_word: jala-mātram prāśya — taking only water; upoṣitāḥ — fasting; tām niśām tatra ūṣuḥ — they spent that night there; nyavasan — remained there
4.translation: After taking only water and observing the fast, they spent the night there.

5.word_for_word: mahān ahiḥ — a great serpent; ajagaraḥ — a python; uragaḥ — ‘one moving on the chest’; urasā gacchan iti alakṣitatvam uktam — its movement upon the breast suggests its stealth; agrasīt jagrāsa — it seized and swallowed
5.translation: The ‘great serpent’ was a python. ‘Uraga,’ literally one that goes upon its breast, also suggests how unnoticed it could approach. It seized Nanda and began swallowing him.

7.word_for_word: vivyadhuḥ — they struck; tāḍayām āsuḥ — beat it; ulmukaiḥ — with firebrands; jvalat-kāṣṭhaiḥ — burning pieces of wood
7.translation: The cowherds struck the serpent repeatedly with burning firebrands.

8.word_for_word: alātaiḥ eva — with those same brands; ulmukaiḥ — burning sticks
8.translation: ‘Alātaiḥ’ again means the burning brands or fire-sticks.

9.word_for_word: vidyādhareṣu arcitam — honored among the Vidyādharas; pūjitam — highly esteemed
9.translation: The released being had been highly honored among the Vidyādharas.

10.word_for_word: gopeṣu ātmanaḥ aiśvaryam prakāśayitum — in order to reveal his majesty before the cowherds; avidvān iva tam apṛcchat — Kṛṣṇa questioned him as though he did not know; dīpyamānena vapuṣā samavasthitam — standing there in a radiant body
10.translation: To make his own omniscient majesty evident to the cowherds through the ensuing answer, Kṛṣṇa questioned the radiant Vidyādhara as though he did not already know who he was.

11.word_for_word: yaḥ parayā śobhayā prakāśate — you who shine with extraordinary beauty; bhavān kaḥ — who are you
11.translation: Kṛṣṇa asks, ‘Who are you, shining with such extraordinary splendor?’

13.word_for_word: prāhasam — I mocked; upahasitavān asmi — I laughed at them; pralabdhaiḥ — with derisive words; upahasitaiḥ — by mockery; madīyena eva pāpena nimittena — because of my own sin alone
13.translation: Sudarśana confesses, ‘I mocked and ridiculed them. What happened to me had its cause in my own sin.’

14.word_for_word: yat yataḥ śāpāt — because of that curse; yataḥ — from which
14.translation: The pronoun refers back to the curse from which his present condition arose.

15.word_for_word: tvā tvām āpṛcche — I ask leave of you; svam lokam gantum anujñām yāce — I request permission to return to my own realm; he amīva-han — O destroyer of affliction/sin; duḥkha-nāśana — O remover of suffering
15.translation: He says, ‘O destroyer of affliction, I now ask your leave and request permission to return to my own celestial realm.’

20.word_for_word: ahi-deham nihatya — having destroyed the serpent body; prāk unmattaṃ sudarśanam — and corrected the formerly proud Sudarśana; tadvat unmādinam śaṅkhacūḍam — similarly the arrogant Śaṅkhacūḍa; kṛṣṇaḥ atāḍayat — Kṛṣṇa struck him; tat-prasaṅgam āha — the narrative now introduces that episode
20.translation: After destroying Sudarśana's serpent form and curing his former arrogance, Kṛṣṇa similarly deals with the intoxicated pride of Śaṅkhacūḍa. The narrative now introduces that episode.

21.word_for_word: virajaḥ-ambarau — the two whose garments were spotless; virajasī nirmale ambare yayoḥ — wearing clean, stainless clothes
21.translation: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are described as wearing pure, spotless garments.

22.word_for_word: niśā-praveśam sat-kurvantau — honoring/welcoming the onset of night; uditāḥ uḍupaḥ tārakāḥ yasmin — when the stars had risen; mallikā-gandhena mattāḥ alayaḥ yasmin — when bees were intoxicated by jasmine fragrance
22.translation: They welcomed the beginning of night, when the stars had appeared and bees were intoxicated by the fragrance of jasmine.

23.word_for_word: anibaddhatvāt — because the notes were not rigidly bound; anyaiḥ yugapat kalpayitum aśakyam api — though impossible for ordinary singers to produce simultaneously; tau svara-maṇḍalasya mūrcchitam yugapat kalpayantau — the two brothers simultaneously unfolded the full modal development of the scale; manaḥ-śravaṇayoḥ maṅgalam — delighting both mind and ear; jagatuḥ agāyatām — they sang
23.translation: Although ordinary singers could not simultaneously unfold such freely moving modal structures, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma together developed the full range of the scale in perfect harmony, singing in a way auspicious and delightful to both mind and ear.

24.word_for_word: mūrcchitāḥ — entranced; tad-gīta-līna-cittāḥ — their minds absorbed in the song; sraṃsat bhraśyat dukūlam — garments slipping down; srastāḥ keśebhyaḥ srajaḥ — garlands falling from their hair; tataḥ na avidan — they no longer noticed these things
24.translation: The women became entranced, their minds dissolved in the brothers' song. Their garments slipped and garlands fell from their hair, but in their absorption they did not even notice.

26.word_for_word: nirīkṣatoḥ — while the two Lords looked on; tau nāthau yasya tam pramadā-janam — the women whose protectors were Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma; kālayām āsa — Śaṅkhacūḍa drove them away; haṭhāt prerayām āsa — forcibly compelled them to move
26.translation: Even while Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were present as their protectors, Śaṅkhacūḍa forcibly drove the women away.

27.word_for_word: dasyunā — by a robber; vyāghreṇa — like a tiger
27.translation: Śaṅkhacūḍa is compared to a robber or predatory tiger carrying off helpless victims.

28.word_for_word: mā bhaiṣṭa — do not fear; bhayam na prāpnuta — be without fear; abhaya-vacau — words granting reassurance
28.translation: The brothers call out words of reassurance: ‘Do not be afraid.’

31.word_for_word: śirasā saha — together with his head; cūḍāmaṇim jagāra — Kṛṣṇa took the crest-jewel
31.translation: Kṛṣṇa severed Śaṅkhacūḍa's head and took the jewel from his crest.
